new.title: Admire the brick Gothic Doberaner Münster
new.desc: The former Cistercian abbey church of Doberan was consecrated in 1368 and is called a pearl of North German brick Gothic. Its interior keeps the 14th-century high altar, a triumphal cross and the tombs of Mecklenburg dukes.
new.tip: Allow an hour for the church and the surrounding monastery grounds. Combine with the Molli railway, which stops a few minutes away.

new.title: See the classicist Kurhaus of Heiligendamm
new.desc: Designed by Carl Theodor Severin and finished in 1816, the Kurhaus is the centrepiece of Germany's oldest seaside resort. It now serves as a restaurant of the Grand Hotel.
new.tip: Walk along the promenade for the best view of the white facade. Non-guests can visit the restaurant.

new.title: Spot Burg Hohenzollern on the Heiligendamm promenade
new.desc: This Tudor-style, castle-like villa was built around 1846 to 1849 and belongs to the Perlenkette, the row of white villas along the seafront. It stands west of the Kurhaus.
new.tip: Seen best from the beach promenade. The villas are private or hotel property, so look from outside.

new.title: Visit the neo-Gothic Herz-Jesu-Waldkapelle
new.desc: This small Catholic brick chapel in the forest near Heiligendamm was built in 1888 in neo-Gothic style. It lies on the quiet path between Heiligendamm and the Kamp area.
new.tip: Opening is irregular, so plan it as a forest-walk stop. The Molli station Heiligendamm is nearby.

new.title: Stroll out on the Kühlungsborn Seebrücke
new.desc: The roughly 240 m long pier is the landmark of Mecklenburg's largest seaside resort. It gives views along the beach promenade and the Bäderarchitektur of the Ostseeallee.
new.tip: Come at sunset. Walk the promenade to see the villas in historic resort style.

new.title: Step into Rerik's early Gothic St. Johannes church
new.desc: St. Johannes is an early Gothic brick church that dominates the old centre of Rerik. It stands close to the Heimatmuseum and the harbour streets.
new.tip: Check opening times posted at the door. The church is a short walk from the Haffpromenade.

new.title: Tour Schloss Güstrow, Mecklenburg's Renaissance showpiece
new.desc: Built from 1558 under Duke Ulrich as the largest preserved Renaissance building in the state, it was later home to the Wallenstein court. Rooms show the State Museum's collections and a Baroque garden of about 4.6 hectares surrounds it.
new.tip: Visit the palace garden in summer. Check the museum hours before travelling.

new.title: See Barlach's Floating Angel in Güstrow Cathedral
new.desc: The Gothic brick cathedral holds Ernst Barlach's bronze angel 'Der Schwebende' from 1927, a memorial to the victims of the First World War. The Nazis removed it on 23 August 1937 as degenerate art; a recast was hung again after the war.
new.tip: Open daily; there is a small donation request. Allow a few minutes to sit under the angel.

new.title: Discover Barlach's work in the Gertrudenkapelle
new.desc: The late Gothic chapel dates from around 1430. Since 1953 it has served as an exhibition space and was the first Barlach museum in Güstrow.
new.tip: Combine with the Dom. The chapel is small, so a short visit is enough.

new.title: Visit Bützow's Stiftskirche with its 1503 altar
new.desc: The three-aisled brick hall church is the landmark of Bützow. It holds a late Gothic winged altar from 1503 and an organ case from around 1510, the oldest in Mecklenburg.
new.tip: Volunteer church guards open it in the warmer months. Ask at the Tourist Information if it is closed.

new.title: Visit Bützow Castle and its museum
new.desc: The castle goes back to a fortress built in 1239 by the bishops of Schwerin and became a Renaissance palace under Duke Ulrich. It received its present form in a rebuilding in 1910/11.
new.tip: Check opening times of the museum before going. It is a short walk from the Stiftskirche.

new.title: Peek into the Krummes Haus in Bützow
new.desc: The Krummes Haus began as a fortification and now houses a library, a museum and a documentation centre. It is part of Bützow's historic centre.
new.tip: Combine with the Stiftskirche and the castle on one walk.

new.title: Visit the Stadtmuseum in Teterow's Malchiner Tor
new.desc: The medieval town gate, the Malchiner Tor, houses the town museum of Teterow. It is one of the surviving parts of the historic town fortification.
new.tip: The museum has seasonal hours, so check ahead. Walk on to the Teterower See.

new.title: Climb the Jörnberg lookout tower at Krakow am See
new.desc: The lookout tower on the Jörnberg gives a panorama over the lakes and forests around Krakow am See. It lies on the edge of the Nossentiner/Schwinzer Heide nature park.
new.tip: Go on a clear day. Bring a jacket since the tower is exposed.

new.title: See the Feldsteinkirche Bellin from around 1230
new.desc: This Late Romanesque fieldstone church near Krakow am See dates from about 1230. It hosts concerts and cultural events during the year.
new.tip: Check the local event calendar for concerts. It is a short drive from Krakow am See.
new.q: Feldsteinkirche Bellin, Bellin, Krakow am See

new.title: See Krakow's Romanesque-Gothic Stadtkirche
new.desc: The brick Stadtkirche is described as the oldest building of Krakow am See. It stands near the neo-Gothic town hall of 1857 and the protected market square.
new.tip: Look at the town hall on the market square too. The lake is a few minutes away.
new.q: Stadtkirche Krakow am See, Krakow am See

new.title: Walk the Rhododendronpark in Graal-Müritz
new.desc: The park of about 4.5 hectares near the beach holds roughly 2,500 rhododendrons and azaleas. It lies at the western end of the promenade.
new.tip: The bloom peaks around May and June. The beach is a few steps away.

new.title: Walk out on the Graal-Müritz Seebrücke
new.desc: The pier reaches more than 300 m into the Baltic Sea and is the centre of the promenade. A beach bar sits directly at its base.
new.tip: Walk the promenade toward the Rhododendronpark. Sunset is the best time.

new.title: Ride the Molli steam railway to Kühlungsborn
new.desc: The narrow-gauge Bäderbahn Molli has run since 1886 through the streets of Bad Doberan to Heiligendamm and, since 1910, to Kühlungsborn. Steam locomotives pull the trains on the 900 mm gauge.
new.tip: Trains run daily; check the timetable on molli-bahn.de. Sit on the left for the sea views after Heiligendamm.
new.q: Molli Bahnhof Bad Doberan, Am Bahnhof, Bad Doberan

new.title: Walk the Heiligendamm Perlenkette promenade
new.desc: The 'Pearl Necklace' is a row of stately white villas along the seafront of Heiligendamm, founded in 1793 as Germany's first seaside resort. The path runs past the Kurhaus to Burg Hohenzollern.
new.tip: Start at the Molli station and walk to the sea. Go early to avoid crowds.

new.title: Swim at the Kühlungsborn beach
new.desc: The long sandy beach along the Ostseeallee is the main bathing area of Kühlungsborn. Beach baskets and a promenade line the shore.
new.tip: Swimming season is summer. Rent a Strandkorb at the pier.

new.title: Stroll the Haffpromenade on the Salzhaff in Rerik
new.desc: The promenade follows the shore of the Salzhaff to the Haffplatz with cafés and restaurants. The lagoon is a popular area for surfing and sailing.
new.tip: Come in the evening for the light over the water. The pier itself is closed for structural reasons.

new.title: Hike the Rerik Steilküste above the Baltic
new.desc: The coastal cliff northeast of Rerik is bordered by a strip of coastal forest and an upper shore path. Trails link on towards the Gespensterwald near Nienhagen.
new.tip: Bring good shoes and stay on the path. The cliff edge is unstable.

new.title: Swim at the Graal-Müritz beach
new.desc: A wide sandy beach with dunes and a pier lies at the heart of the seaside resort. Beach bars and a promenade are close.
new.tip: Swimming is a summer activity. Walk the promenade afterwards.

new.title: Walk the Ribnitzer Großes Moor near Graal-Müritz
new.desc: The nature reserve east of Graal-Müritz is a raised bog about 6,000 years old. A path leads through the bog landscape.
new.tip: Wear sturdy shoes and bring insect repellent in summer.

new.title: Hike the Gespensterwald by the Baltic cliff
new.desc: The 180-hectare Ghost Forest near Nienhagen has trees bent into strange shapes by salty sea wind. A trail leads along the cliff.
new.tip: Walk in the morning or on a misty day. Stay on the marked path.

new.title: Meet native animals in Wildpark-MV near Güstrow
new.desc: The park covers about 200 hectares and has been open since 1959. It has animal programmes, a petting zoo, trails and an aqua tunnel to watch animals underwater.
new.tip: Plan half a day. Check seasonal hours before travelling.

new.title: Paddle a kayak or SUP at Krakow's Borgwall
new.desc: Rowboats, kayaks and SUPs can be rented at the Am Borgwall area on the Krakower See, depending on availability.
new.tip: Go on weekdays for the best availability.

new.title: Walk the Burgwallinsel in Teterow
new.desc: The Burgwallinsel in the Teterower See is a former Slavic fortress site reached by a footbridge. It is part of the lakeside walks of the town.
new.tip: Combine with the Malchiner Tor and a lap around the lake.

new.title: Dine at Villa Astoria on the Ostseeallee
new.desc: The restaurant of chef Tillmann Hahn is known as one of the best in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. He cooked at the 2007 G8 summit in Heiligendamm.
new.tip: Reserve ahead and order the regional fish menu.

new.title: Grill by the sea at Strandauster, Kühlungsborn
new.desc: The restaurant on the Ostseeallee serves regional and international food and has a summer grill terrace and an Art Nouveau bar.
new.tip: Order grilled fish on the terrace.

new.title: Eat Baltic fish at Zur Reuse, Kühlungsborn
new.desc: The restaurant prepares Baltic fish with traditional Mecklenburg recipes.
new.tip: Choose the catch of the day.

new.title: Scoop ice cream at Janny's Eis, Kühlungsborn
new.desc: The ice cream parlour in Hermannstraße is praised for large scoops and creative flavours.
new.tip: Try a seasonal flavour after a beach walk.

new.title: Taste smoked fish at Erlebnisräucherei Scheller, Rerik
new.desc: The fishery R. Scheller runs a smokehouse near the Salzhaff with a seafood restaurant, rated 4.8 by almost 2,000 reviewers.
new.tip: Try freshly smoked eel or Baltic herring.

new.title: Eat fresh fish at Harry's Fischerhütte, Rerik
new.desc: The fish hut on the Haffpromenade is rated 4.8 stars, and guests praise the preparation of fish.
new.tip: Closed Mondays. Order the fried Baltic fish.

new.title: Dine on Baltic fish at Restaurant Wallenstein, Güstrow
new.desc: The hotel restaurant on the edge of the old town looks over the castle. It serves fish from the Baltic and Bodden plus Mecklenburg dishes.
new.tip: Book a window table for the castle view.

new.title: Order Mecklenburg plum roast at Schröders, Güstrow
new.desc: The restaurant Schröders in the Kurhaus am Inselsee has a Mecklenburg profile, including Pflaumenbraten with red cabbage and potato dumplings.
new.tip: Ask for a lake-side table and walk the Inselsee afterwards.

new.title: Eat fish at Fischrestaurant Zur Boje, Graal-Müritz
new.desc: Zur Boje is ranked among the top fish restaurants of the resort in a user-review directory.
new.tip: Order the fresh Baltic fish.

new.title: Have homemade cake at Caféstübchen Witt, Graal-Müritz
new.desc: The café and pension at Am Tannenhof 2 offers breakfast, fresh fish, Mecklenburg dishes and homemade cake.
new.tip: Come for cake after the beach.
new.q: Caféstübchen und Pension Witt, Am Tannenhof 2, Graal-Müritz
